questions.question: How much money was allotted by the Gujarat government in August 2023 for the One District, One Product (ODOP) Programme to promote its indigenous products at the international level?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**₹58 crore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In August 2023, the Gujarat government allocated **₹58 crores** for the **One District, One Product (ODOP)** programme to promote indigenous products at the international level.
 
• The ODOP initiative aims to identify and promote unique products from each district, enhancing their market reach and economic potential.
 
• Under this scheme, more than 25 handicraft products from 21 districts, including traditional crafts like **Gamthi Block Print** and **Mata-ni-Pachedi**, have been selected for promotion.
 
• The Gujarat State Handicrafts and Handloom Development Corporation (GSHHDC) is responsible for implementing the ODOP scheme in the state.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **One District, One Product (ODOP):** A government initiative aimed at fostering balanced regional development by identifying and promoting unique products from each district.
 
• **Gujarat State Handicrafts and Handloom Development Corporation (GSHHDC):** An organization dedicated to the development and promotion of handicrafts and handlooms in Gujarat.
 
• **Gamthi Block Print:** A traditional hand-block printing technique from Gujarat, known for its intricate designs and vibrant colors.
 
• **Mata-ni-Pachedi:** A traditional art form from Gujarat involving hand-painted or block-printed cloth used as a backdrop in temples.
 
• **International Promotion:** The ODOP scheme includes strategies to enhance the global visibility and marketability of selected products through branding, exhibitions, and e-commerce platforms.
 
• **Economic Empowerment:** By promoting district-specific products, the ODOP initiative aims to boost local economies, create employment opportunities, and preserve traditional crafts.

questions.question: In the context of microfinance in India, the concept of SHG-BLP is used. What does L stand for in SHG-BLP?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Linkage**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• SHG-BLP stands for **Self-Help Group - Bank Linkage Programme**.
 
• This programme was initiated by the **NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development)** in 1992.
 
• The primary objective of the SHG-BLP is to **provide financial services to the rural poor** through the linkage of self-help groups with banks.
 
• It aims to **improve the socio-economic status** of the rural poor, particularly women, by providing access to formal banking services.
 
• The programme has been **instrumental in promoting financial inclusion** and empowering women across rural India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **NABARD**

 
 
• NABARD is the apex development bank in India with a mandate to facilitate credit flow for the promotion and development of agriculture, small-scale industries, cottage and village industries, handicrafts, and other rural crafts.
 
• It was established on **12 July 1982** by an act of the Parliament.
 
• NABARD's mission is to promote sustainable and equitable agriculture and rural development through participative financial and non-financial interventions, innovations, technology, and institutional development.
 
 
 
• **Self-Help Groups (SHGs)**
 
 
• SHGs are small voluntary associations of people, preferably from the same socio-economic background.
 
• The primary aim is to promote savings and thrift among members and provide loans to meet their credit needs.
 
• SHGs are usually formed around a common activity or purpose, such as farming, handicrafts, or small enterprises.
 
 
 
• **Financial Inclusion**
 
 
• Financial inclusion refers to the process of ensuring access to financial services and timely and adequate credit where needed by vulnerable groups such as weaker sections and low-income groups at an affordable cost.
 
• It aims to address and offer solutions to the constraints that exclude people from participating in the financial sector.
 
 
 
• **Women Empowerment**
 
 
• The SHG-BLP has been particularly successful in empowering women by providing them with financial independence.
 
• Women SHGs have contributed significantly to improving household incomes and community development.

questions.question: In which among the following years was Hindu widow remarriage declared legal in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1856**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act, 1856 was enacted on 26 July 1856.
 
• The Act was formulated to legalize the remarriage of Hindu widows in India.
 
• This legislation was a significant social reform during British rule in India.
 
• It was largely advocated by social reformers such as Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar.
 
• The Act aimed to improve the condition of Hindu widows who were traditionally not allowed to remarry.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar:**

 
 
• He was a prominent Indian educator and social reformer.
 
• He played a crucial role in the enactment of the Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act, 1856.
 
• His efforts were pivotal in challenging orthodox Hindu society and promoting widow remarriage.
 
 
 
• **The Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act, 1856:**
 
 
• The Act provided legal safeguards and rights to widows who chose to remarry.
 
• It also annulled the stigma and social ostracism faced by widows for remarrying.
 
 
 
• **Social Impact:**
 
 
• The enactment of the Act marked a progressive step towards the modernization of Indian society.
 
• It laid the foundation for further social reforms concerning women's rights in India.
 
 
 
• **British India's Social Reforms:**
 
 
• The 19th century saw several social reforms initiated under British rule, addressing various social issues.
 
• These reforms included the abolition of Sati and the promotion of education among women.
tags: Socio - Religious Reform Movements in the 19th and 20th CE India

questions.question: Annapurna Devi is associated with which of the following musical instruments?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Surbahar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Annapurna Devi was a renowned Indian classical musician known for her mastery of the Surbahar, a bass version of the sitar.
 
• She was the daughter of Ustad Allauddin Khan, a legendary musician and founder of the Maihar Gharana.
 
• Annapurna Devi was married to the famous sitar virtuoso Ravi Shankar.
 
• Despite her immense talent, she performed publicly only on rare occasions, dedicating most of her life to teaching music.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Surbahar**

 
 
• Also known as the bass sitar, it produces a deeper and more resonant sound compared to the sitar.
 
• It is primarily used for performing the dhrupad style of Indian classical music.
 
• The Surbahar typically has a longer neck and larger gourd than the sitar.
 
 
 
• **Maihar Gharana**
 
 
• A prominent school of Indian classical music founded by Ustad Allauddin Khan.
 
• It has produced several legendary musicians, including Ravi Shankar and Ali Akbar Khan.
 
 
 
• **Dhrupad**
 
 
• One of the oldest forms of North Indian classical music.
 
• Characterized by its spiritual and meditative nature, it is often performed with the Surbahar.
 
 
 
• **Ustad Allauddin Khan**
 
 
• A legendary musician and founder of the Maihar Gharana.
 
• He was a multi-instrumentalist and a highly respected guru.

questions.question: Who regarded Vedas as the source of all knowledge and known for the slogan 'Go back to the Vedas'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Swami Dayananda Saraswati**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Swami Dayananda Saraswati** was a social reformer and founder of the **Arya Samaj**, a Hindu reform movement.
 
• He promoted the idea that the **Vedas are the ultimate source of knowledge** and called for a return to their teachings.
 
• His famous slogan, **"Go back to the Vedas,"** emphasized the revival of ancient Hindu wisdom and rejection of idol worship and superstitions.
 
• He worked towards religious and social reforms, advocating for women's rights, education, and the abolition of caste-based discrimination.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Arya Samaj:** Founded by Swami Dayananda in 1875, it aimed at reviving Vedic traditions and opposing rituals that were not found in the Vedas.
 
• **Rejection of Idol Worship:** He strongly opposed idol worship, polytheism, and social evils, advocating monotheism based on the Vedas.
 
• **Education Reforms:** He emphasized the importance of Vedic education and established several gurukuls to promote Sanskrit and Vedic learning.
 
• **Social Reforms:** Swami Dayananda championed causes such as widow remarriage, women's education, and the abolition of untouchability.
 
• **Satyarth Prakash:** His famous book, *Satyarth Prakash*, contained his interpretation of the Vedas and outlined his vision for religious and social reforms.
 
• His teachings greatly influenced the Indian independence movement, inspiring leaders like **Lala Lajpat Rai** and other nationalists who saw his call for a return to Vedic values as a foundation for self-reliance and social unity.

questions.question: What is the length of the men's kabaddi court?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**13 m**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The length of the men's kabaddi court is **13 meters**.
 
• The width of the men's kabaddi court is **10 meters**.
 
• These dimensions are specified by the **International Kabaddi Federation (IKF)**.
 
• The court is divided into two equal halves by a midline, each half measuring **6.5 meters by 10 meters**.
 
• The kabaddi court dimensions are the same for both indoor and outdoor play.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kabaddi**

 
 
• It is a contact team sport that originated in ancient India.
 
• Kabaddi is popular in South Asia and has gained international recognition.
 
• The game involves two teams of seven players each, with the objective of scoring points by raiding the opponent's half and tagging as many defenders as possible without getting caught.
 
• The sport requires a combination of strength, strategy, and agility.
 
 
 
• **Pro Kabaddi League (PKL)**
 
 
• It is a professional kabaddi league in India, founded in 2014.
 
• The league follows a franchise-based model, similar to the Indian Premier League (IPL) in cricket.
 
• PKL has significantly increased the popularity and viewership of kabaddi in India and around the world.
 
• The league has helped in professionalizing the sport and providing a platform for talented players.
 
 
 
• **International Kabaddi Federation (IKF)**
 
 
• It is the global governing body for the sport of kabaddi.
 
• IKF organizes international tournaments and works towards promoting and standardizing kabaddi worldwide.
 
• The federation ensures that the rules and regulations of the sport are uniformly followed across member countries.
 
• IKF also aims to include kabaddi in the Olympic Games in the future.
 
 
 
• **Asian Games**
 
 
• Kabaddi has been a part of the Asian Games since 1990.
 
• India has been the most successful country in kabaddi at the Asian Games, winning multiple gold medals.
 
• The inclusion of kabaddi in the Asian Games has helped in increasing its popularity across Asia.
 
• Both men's and women's kabaddi competitions are held at the Asian Games.

questions.question: Which of the given options is rod-shaped, carries genetic information, is visible only at cell division and is present in the nucleus?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chromosomes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Chromosomes** are rod-shaped structures that are found in the nucleus of eukaryotic cells.
 
• They carry genetic information in the form of genes, which are responsible for heredity and variations in living organisms.
 
• Chromosomes are visible only during cell division, particularly in the metaphase stage of mitosis and meiosis.
 
• Each chromosome is made up of DNA tightly coiled many times around proteins called histones that support its structure.
 
• In humans, there are 23 pairs of chromosomes, totaling 46 chromosomes in each somatic cell.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **DNA (Deoxyribonucleic Acid)**

 
 
• DNA is the hereditary material in humans and almost all other organisms.
 
• Most DNA is located in the cell nucleus (nuclear DNA) and a small amount in mitochondria (mitochondrial DNA).
 
• DNA is composed of two strands that coil around each other to form a double helix.
 
• It carries the genetic instructions used in the growth, development, functioning, and reproduction of all known living organisms.
 
 
 
• **Histones**
 
 
• Histones are highly alkaline proteins found in eukaryotic cell nuclei.
 
• They package and order the DNA into structural units called nucleosomes.
 
• Histones play a role in gene regulation.
 
 
 
• **Cell Division**
 
 
• Cell division is the process by which a parent cell divides into two or more daughter cells.
 
• Mitosis and meiosis are two types of cell division in eukaryotes.
 
• Mitosis results in two identical daughter cells, while meiosis results in four genetically different daughter cells.
 
 
 
• **Genetic Variation**
 
 
• Genetic variation refers to the diversity in gene frequencies.
 
• It can be caused by mutation, random mating, random fertilization, and recombination between homologous chromosomes during meiosis.
 
• Genetic variation is crucial for a population's ability to adapt to changing environments.

questions.question: Prerana Shrimali received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in which of the following years for her contribution to the Kathak dance form?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2009**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Prerana Shrimali is a renowned Kathak dancer recognized for her contributions to the classical dance form.
 
• She received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 2009 for her exceptional work in Kathak.
 
• The Sangeet Natak Akademi Award is one of the highest Indian recognition given to practicing artists.
 
• Prerana Shrimali has been instrumental in propagating and preserving the Kathak dance form through her performances and teachings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sangeet Natak Akademi**

 
 
• Established in 1952, it is the national academy for music, dance, and drama in India.
 
• The Akademi honors artists with awards and fellowships for their outstanding contributions to their respective fields.
 
• It plays a crucial role in the preservation, promotion, and development of the performing arts in India.
 
• The Akademi also organizes various festivals, seminars, and exhibitions to showcase traditional and contemporary arts.
 
 
 
• **Kathak**
 
 
• One of the eight major classical dance forms of India.
 
• Originated from the wandering bards of ancient northern India known as Kathakars or storytellers.
 
• It is characterized by intricate footwork, spins, and expressive gestures and facial expressions.
 
• Kathak has evolved over the centuries and incorporates elements from both Hindu and Muslim cultures.
 
 
 
• **Other notable Kathak dancers**
 
 
• Brijmohan Mishra (Birju Maharaj)
 
• Shovana Narayan
 
• Kumudini Lakhia
 
• Maya Rao
 
 
 
• **Importance of Awards in Arts**
 
 
• Awards like the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award provide recognition and encouragement to artists.
 
• They help in preserving and promoting traditional art forms.
 
• Awards contribute to the cultural richness and heritage of a nation.
 
• They also inspire the younger generation to pursue and excel in various art forms.

questions.question: Which gas is released when you combine vinegar and baking soda in a balloon, causing it to inflate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Carbon dioxide**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When vinegar (acetic acid) reacts with baking soda (sodium bicarbonate), it produces carbon dioxide gas.
 
• This reaction is an example of an acid-base reaction, which results in the formation of a gas, water, and a salt (sodium acetate).
 
• The carbon dioxide gas produced in the reaction gets trapped in the balloon, causing it to inflate.
 
• The chemical equation for this reaction is: CH₃COOH + NaHCO₃ → CO₂ + H₂O + CH₃COONa.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vinegar**:

 
 
• Vinegar is a dilute solution of acetic acid (CH₃COOH) in water.
 
• It is commonly used in cooking, cleaning, and as a preservative.
 
 
 
• **Baking Soda**:
 
 
• Baking soda, or sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO₃), is a weak base.
 
• It is used in baking as a leavening agent, in cleaning, and for medical purposes.
 
 
 
• **Carbon Dioxide (CO₂)**:
 
 
• Carbon dioxide is a colorless, odorless gas that is naturally present in the Earth's atmosphere.
 
• It is produced by the respiration of animals and the combustion of fossil fuels.
 
• CO₂ is also used in carbonated beverages and as a refrigerant.
 
 
 
• **Acid-Base Reactions**:
 
 
• These reactions involve the reaction of an acid with a base to produce a salt and water.
 
• Acid-base reactions are fundamental chemical reactions with wide applications in chemistry and industry.

questions.question: From 13 September 2023, DMK MP Tiruchi Siva has been appointed the chairperson of the Committee on ____________
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Industry**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• From 13 September 2023, DMK MP Tiruchi Siva has been appointed as the chairperson of the Committee on **Industry**.
 
• The Committee on Industry is responsible for examining issues related to various industrial sectors in India.
 
• The appointment of Tiruchi Siva aims to provide better oversight and strategic guidance for the industrial sector.
 
• This committee plays a crucial role in reviewing industrial policies and making recommendations to the government.
 
• It is one of the several parliamentary committees formed to scrutinize and oversee different sectors of governance and public administration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Parliamentary Committees**

 
 
• Parliamentary committees are formed to handle the work of Parliament more efficiently and effectively.
 
• They examine bills, budgets, and policies in detail and make recommendations.
 
• Standing committees are permanent and divided into various categories such as finance, health, and industry.
 
• Ad hoc committees are temporary and formed for specific tasks.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Committee on Industry**
 
 
• It scrutinizes the functioning of industrial units and suggests improvements.
 
• It reviews the performance of public sector enterprises and their impact on the economy.
 
• The committee assesses the implementation of industrial policies and their alignment with national goals.
 
• It interacts with industry representatives to understand their challenges and opportunities.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Industrial Sector in India**
 
 
• The industrial sector is a major contributor to India's GDP.
 
• It includes manufacturing, mining, construction, and utilities.
 
• Industrial growth is critical for job creation and economic development.
 
• Government policies like Make in India aim to boost industrial production and attract investments.
 
 
 
• **Recent Government Initiatives for Industry**
 
 
• Production Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes to boost manufacturing.
 
• Ease of Doing Business reforms to simplify regulatory processes.
 
• Infrastructure development to support industrial growth.
 
• Special Economic Zones (SEZs) to promote exports and investment.

questions.question: Which of the following Rights is mentioned in Article 21 of the Indian Constitution?

options.text: Right to Freedom: Protection of life and personal liberty
Right against Exploitation: Prohibition of trafficking in human beings and forced labour
Right to Equality: Equality before law
Right to Freedom of Religion: Freedom to manage religious affairs

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Right to Freedom: Protection of life and personal liberty**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 21 of the Indian Constitution guarantees the **Right to Protection of life and personal liberty** to all citizens and non-citizens.
 
• It states, "No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law."
 
• This article ensures that the State cannot take away a person's life or liberty arbitrarily without following due process of law.
 
• It encompasses a wide range of rights, including the right to live with human dignity, right to privacy, and right to a healthy environment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Right to Privacy**

 
 
• In the landmark judgment of *Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd.) vs Union of India* (2017), the Supreme Court of India declared the right to privacy as a fundamental right under Article 21.
 
• This judgment has significant implications for data protection and individual autonomy in India.
 
 
 
• **Right to a Healthy Environment**
 
 
• Article 21 has been interpreted by the judiciary to include the right to a pollution-free environment, which is essential for living a quality life.
 
• Environmental protection and sustainability have been integrated into the right to life and personal liberty.
 
 
 
• **Right to Legal Aid**
 
 
• The right to free legal aid is considered an integral part of Article 21 to ensure that justice is accessible to all, irrespective of economic status.
 
• The Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, implements this right by providing free legal services to the weaker sections of society.
 
 
 
• **Right to Live with Human Dignity**
 
 
• The Supreme Court has expanded Article 21 to include the right to live with dignity, which encompasses adequate nutrition, clothing, shelter, and proper healthcare.
 
• This broader interpretation aims at ensuring a decent standard of living for every individual.

questions.question: The Sahitya Akademi award winning novel 'Zindaginama' was written by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Krishna Sobti**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Krishna Sobti was awarded the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1980 for her novel **'Zindaginama.'**
 
• 'Zindaginama' is considered one of her most significant works and portrays the socio-cultural landscape of rural Punjab.
 
• Krishna Sobti is known for her profound impact on contemporary Hindi literature and her distinct narrative style.
 
• She was also honored with the prestigious Jnanpith Award in 2017 for her contribution to Indian literature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sahitya Akademi Award**

 
 
• Established in 1954, it is a literary honor in India which recognizes outstanding books of literary merit.
 
• The award is presented annually by the Sahitya Akademi, India's National Academy of Letters.
 
• It covers works in 24 languages recognized by the Sahitya Akademi, including Hindi, English, and regional languages.
 
• The award includes a plaque and a cash prize of Rs. 1,00,000.
 
 
 
• **Krishna Sobti's Literary Contributions**
 
 
• She wrote several acclaimed novels including 'Mitro Marjani,' 'Surajmukhi Andhere Ke,' and 'Samay Sargam.'
 
• Her writing often explores themes of identity, gender, and the human condition.
 
• Sobti's works are known for their rich linguistic texture and deep psychological insight.
 
 
 
• **Jnanpith Award**
 
 
• It is the highest literary honor in India, awarded annually by the Bharatiya Jnanpith.
 
• Established in 1961, the award recognizes distinguished literary work in any of the languages included in the Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Winners receive a cash prize, a citation plaque, and a bronze replica of Saraswati, the Hindu goddess of knowledge and arts.
 
 
 
• **Hindi Literature**
 
 
• Hindi literature comprises literary works written primarily in Hindi, a major language in India.
 
• It includes various forms such as poetry, novels, short stories, and plays.
 
• Notable Hindi literary figures include Premchand, Mahadevi Verma, Harivansh Rai Bachchan, and Nirmal Verma.

questions.question: Who among the following is worshipped as Nataraja before many classical dance performances in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shiva**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Shiva, known as Nataraja, is worshipped as the divine cosmic dancer before many classical dance performances in India.
 
• The term Nataraja translates to "King of Dance" (nata meaning dance, and raja meaning king).
 
• The Nataraja form of Shiva is depicted with four arms, dancing within a circle of flames, symbolizing the cosmic cycles of creation and destruction.
 
• Shiva's dance represents the dynamic and rhythmic movement of the universe and is an important motif in Indian arts and culture.
 
• Classical dance forms like Bharatanatyam and Odissi often begin with an invocation to Nataraja, seeking blessings for a successful performance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Iconography of Nataraja**

 
 
• The Nataraja statue typically shows Shiva dancing on the demon Apasmara, symbolizing the triumph over ignorance.
 
• His upper right hand holds a drum (damaru), representing the sound of creation.
 
• The upper left hand holds fire, symbolizing destruction and transformation.
 
• His lower right hand is in the abhaya mudra, meaning protection and assurance.
 
• The lower left hand points to his raised left foot, signifying liberation and salvation.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance**
 
 
• The concept of Nataraja dates back to the Chola dynasty (9th to 13th century CE) in South India, where it became a central icon of the Chola art.
 
• Bronze sculptures of Nataraja from this period are considered masterpieces of Indian art.
 
• The Chidambaram Temple in Tamil Nadu is one of the most famous temples dedicated to Nataraja.
 
 
 
• **Philosophical Interpretations**
 
 
• Shiva's dance is seen as a symbol of the cosmic cycles of creation, preservation, and dissolution.
 
• It also represents the five activities (panchakritya): creation (srishti), preservation (sthiti), destruction (samhara), concealment (tirodhana), and grace (anugraha).
 
• The dance is also a metaphor for the inner dance of the human soul and the divine.
 
 
 
• **Role in Indian Classical Dance**
 
 
• Invoking Nataraja is a tradition in many classical dance forms like Bharatanatyam, Kathak, and Odissi.
 
• This invocation is meant to seek the deity's blessings for the success and sanctity of the performance.
 
• It also highlights the spiritual aspect of dance, viewing it as a divine art form.

questions.question: The famous 'Tripartite struggle' for supremacy occurred between which of the following powers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gurjar-Pratihara, Rashtrakuta and Palas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Tripartite Struggle was a prolonged conflict during the 8th to 10th centuries.
 
• It involved three major dynasties: the Gurjar-Pratiharas, the Rashtrakutas, and the Palas.
 
• The main objective of this struggle was to gain control over the fertile region of Kannauj.
 
• Kannauj was a significant cultural and political center during this period.
 
• The struggle significantly impacted the political landscape of Northern and Central India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gurjar-Pratihara Dynasty**

 
 
• The Gurjar-Pratiharas were known for their strong defense against Arab invasions in Western India.
 
• Their capital was initially at Ujjain and later at Kannauj.
 
• The dynasty reached its zenith under the rule of Mihira Bhoja.
 
 
 
• **Rashtrakuta Dynasty**
 
 
• The Rashtrakutas were a prominent dynasty in the Deccan region with their capital at Manyakheta.
 
• They are known for their patronage of art and architecture, including the famous Ellora caves.
 
• Their rule extended over large parts of South and Central India.
 
 
 
• **Pala Dynasty**
 
 
• The Palas ruled over the Bengal region and were known for their contribution to Buddhism.
 
• They established the famous Vikramashila and Nalanda universities.
 
• The dynasty was founded by Gopala in the 8th century.
 
 
 
• **Kannauj**
 
 
• Kannauj, located in present-day Uttar Pradesh, was a significant city in ancient India.
 
• It was strategically important due to its location on the Ganges river and fertile lands.
 
• Control over Kannauj was crucial for political supremacy in Northern India.

questions.question: Four resistors of equal resistance R each are connected in various possible ways both in series and/or parallel to get different combined resistances. Which of the following values of resistance cannot be achieved by using all the four resistors?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2 R**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Four equal resistors (R) can be connected in series or parallel to achieve specific resistance values.
 
• In a series connection, the total resistance (R_total) is the sum of individual resistances: R_total = R + R + R + R = 4R.
 
• In a parallel connection, the total resistance (R_total) is given by 1/R_total = 1/R + 1/R + 1/R + 1/R = 1/0.25R = 0.25R.
 
• Combinations of series and parallel connections can yield intermediate resistance values, but 2R cannot be achieved.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Series Circuit:**

 
 
• Resistors are connected end-to-end, and the current flows through each resistor sequentially.
 
• The total resistance is the sum of all individual resistances.
 
• Suitable for applications where the same current needs to pass through each component.
 
 
 
• **Parallel Circuit:**
 
 
• Resistors are connected across the same two points, creating multiple paths for the current.
 
• The total resistance is lower than the smallest individual resistance in the circuit.
 
• Used in electrical wiring to ensure that each component operates independently of others.
 
 
 
• **Combination Circuits:**
 
 
• Involves both series and parallel connections within the same circuit.
 
• Allows for more complex resistance values and control over current distribution.
 
• Used in advanced electronic devices and complex electrical systems.
 
 
 
• **Ohm's Law:**
 
 
• States that the current (I) through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage (V) across the two points and inversely proportional to the resistance (R).
 
• Mathematically represented as V = IR.
 
• Fundamental to understanding and calculating values in electrical circuits.

questions.question: The remains of Great Bath have been found from the excavation at which of the following Harappan sites?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mohenjodaro**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Great Bath was discovered at the archaeological site of **Mohenjodaro**, one of the most prominent sites of the Indus Valley Civilization.
 
• Mohenjodaro is located in the Sindh province of present-day **Pakistan**.
 
• The Great Bath is one of the best-known structures among the ruins of Mohenjodaro and is believed to have been used for ritualistic purposes.
 
• This structure measures approximately **12 meters long, 7 meters wide, and 2.4 meters deep** and is made of baked bricks.
 
• The Great Bath is an early example of **public water management** and intricate hydraulic engineering.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indus Valley Civilization**

 
 
• Also known as the Harappan Civilization, it flourished around 2500 BCE in the northwestern regions of South Asia.
 
• It is noted for its advanced urban planning, architecture, and social organization.
 
• Key sites include Harappa, Mohenjodaro, Dholavira, and Lothal.
 
 
 
• **Mohenjodaro**
 
 
• It was one of the largest cities of the Indus Valley Civilization and a UNESCO World Heritage site.
 
• The city featured a well-planned grid layout, advanced drainage system, and standardized brick sizes.
 
• Mohenjodaro means "Mound of the Dead" in Sindhi.
 
 
 
• **Great Bath**
 
 
• It is considered one of the earliest public water tanks in the ancient world.
 
• The structure had a layer of natural bitumen to make it waterproof.
 
• Steps at either end of the bath indicate that it was used for ceremonial bathing.
 
 
 
• **Excavation of Mohenjodaro**
 
 
• The site was first discovered by R. D. Banerji in 1922.
 
• Subsequent excavations were carried out by John Marshall, Ernest Mackay, and others.
 
• Excavations revealed a wealth of artifacts including pottery, tools, and seals.

questions.question: As per HDI 2021, which of the following neighbouring countries of India had the highest female life expectancy at birth?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maldives**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As per the Human Development Index (HDI) 2021, Maldives had the highest female life expectancy at birth among India's neighboring countries.
 
• Female life expectancy at birth in the Maldives was approximately 80.3 years in 2021.
 
• The HDI report is published by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP).
 
• Life expectancy at birth is a key component of the HDI, reflecting the overall health and longevity of a population.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Human Development Index (HDI)**

 
 
• The HDI is a composite index measuring average achievement in three basic dimensions of human development: a long and healthy life, knowledge, and a decent standard of living.
 
• The HDI is published annually by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP).
 
• Life expectancy at birth is used to measure the dimension of a long and healthy life.
 
• Education is measured by mean years of schooling and expected years of schooling.
 
• Gross National Income (GNI) per capita is used to measure the standard of living dimension.
 
 
 
• **Life Expectancy at Birth**
 
 
• Life expectancy at birth indicates the number of years a newborn infant would live if prevailing patterns of mortality at the time of birth were to stay the same throughout its life.
 
• It is a crucial indicator of the overall health and longevity of a population.
 
• Factors influencing life expectancy include healthcare quality, lifestyle, and socio-economic conditions.
 
 
 
• **Health Indicators in Maldives**
 
 
• Maldives has made significant progress in healthcare, resulting in high life expectancy rates.
 
• Key health indicators include low maternal and infant mortality rates, and high immunization coverage.
 
• The Maldives government has invested substantially in healthcare infrastructure and services.

questions.question: What is the retirement age of Judges serving at the Supreme Court of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**65 years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The retirement age of Judges serving at the Supreme Court of India is **65 years**.
 
• This age limit is established to ensure a balance between experience and the need for fresh perspectives.
 
• Judges of the Supreme Court are appointed until they reach the age of 65, as per the Constitution of India.
 
• After retirement, former Supreme Court judges may be appointed to other judicial roles, such as in tribunals or commissions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Constitutional Provisions:**

 
 
• Article 124 of the Indian Constitution deals with the establishment and constitution of the Supreme Court.
 
• Article 124(2) specifies that every Judge of the Supreme Court shall hold office until they attain the age of 65 years.
 
 
 
• **Appointment of Judges:**
 
 
• Supreme Court judges are appointed by the President of India.
 
• The Chief Justice of India is appointed based on seniority and consultation with other judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts.
 
 
 
• **Post-Retirement Roles:**
 
 
• Retired judges may be appointed to various commissions, tribunals, or as heads of inquiry committees.
 
• They may also serve as arbitrators in legal disputes.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with High Court Judges:**
 
 
• High Court judges in India retire at the age of 62.
 
• This difference in retirement age helps to maintain a pool of experienced judges who may be elevated to the Supreme Court.

questions.question: According to the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare 2022-23, which state of India is the largest producer of sugarcane?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uttar Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Uttar Pradesh is the largest producer of sugarcane in India, according to the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare 2022-23.
 
• It contributes approximately 38% of the total sugarcane production in the country.
 
• The state has a favorable climate and fertile soil, which are ideal for sugarcane cultivation.
 
• The major sugarcane-producing regions in Uttar Pradesh include Western and Central parts of the state.
 
• Uttar Pradesh also has a significant number of sugar mills, aiding in the production and processing of sugarcane.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sugarcane Varieties**

 
 
• Different varieties of sugarcane are grown in India, including Co 0238, Co 86032, and Co 0118, which are known for their high yield and sugar content.
 
• These varieties are developed by various agricultural research institutes to improve productivity and disease resistance.
 
 
 
• **Sugarcane By-products**
 
 
• By-products of sugarcane include molasses, bagasse, and press mud.
 
• Molasses is used in the production of ethanol, bagasse is used as a biofuel, and press mud is used as a soil amendment.
 
 
 
• **Sugarcane Processing**
 
 
• Sugarcane processing involves crushing the cane to extract juice, which is then boiled to produce sugar crystals.
 
• The process also involves clarification, evaporation, crystallization, and centrifugation.
 
 
 
• **Economic Impact**
 
 
• Sugarcane farming is a significant source of income for millions of farmers in India.
 
• The sugar industry contributes substantially to the rural economy and employment.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives**
 
 
• The Indian government supports sugarcane farmers through various schemes, including subsidies and minimum support prices.
 
• Research and development initiatives are undertaken to improve crop yield and sustainability.

questions.question: Which of the following peaks is NOT located in the Himalayan mountains?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kalsubai**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Kalsubai is the highest peak in Maharashtra, located in the Western Ghats.
 
• It is not a part of the Himalayan mountain range.
 
• The peak stands at an elevation of 1,646 meters (5,400 feet) above sea level.
 
• Kalsubai is situated in the Ahmednagar district and is a popular trekking destination.
 
• The other peaks listed (Nanda Devi, Kamet, and Annapurna) are all located in the Himalayan mountains.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nanda Devi**

 
 
• It is the second highest mountain in India, located in the Garhwal Himalayas in the state of Uttarakhand.
 
• It stands at an elevation of 7,816 meters (25,643 feet).
 
• Nanda Devi is part of the Nanda Devi National Park, which is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
 
 
• **Kamet**
 
 
• Kamet is the second highest mountain in the Garhwal region of Uttarakhand, India.
 
• It has an elevation of 7,756 meters (25,446 feet).
 
• Kamet is part of the Zanskar Range in the Himalayas.
 
 
 
• **Annapurna**
 
 
• Annapurna is a mountain massif in the Himalayas located in north-central Nepal.
 
• It includes one peak over 8,000 meters—Annapurna I Main, which stands at 8,091 meters (26,545 feet).
 
• The Annapurna Conservation Area is the largest protected area in Nepal.

questions.question: Chithirai festival of Tamil Nadu is dedicated to which of the following Goddesses?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Meenakshi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Chithirai festival, also known as Chithirai Thiruvizha, is one of the biggest and most significant festivals in Tamil Nadu.
 
• This festival is dedicated to Goddess Meenakshi, an avatar of Goddess Parvati, and her celestial wedding to Lord Sundareswarar (an incarnation of Lord Shiva).
 
• The festival is celebrated annually in the Tamil month of Chithirai (April-May) in the city of Madurai, which is home to the famous Meenakshi Amman Temple.
 
• The Chithirai festival spans over a month, with the first 15 days dedicated to Goddess Meenakshi's coronation and wedding, followed by the celebration of Lord Alagar's (Vishnu) journey from Alagar Koyil to Madurai.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Meenakshi Amman Temple**

 
 
• The Meenakshi Amman Temple is one of the most famous temples in India, known for its remarkable architecture and historical significance.
 
• The temple complex is spread over 14 acres and has 14 gopurams (gateway towers), the tallest being 170 feet.
 
• The temple is a major pilgrimage destination and attracts millions of devotees and tourists annually.
 
 
 
• **Goddess Meenakshi**
 
 
• Goddess Meenakshi is considered an incarnation of Goddess Parvati and is worshipped as the divine queen of Madurai.
 
• She is often depicted with a parrot in her right hand and a sword in her left hand, symbolizing wisdom and valor.
 
 
 
• **Chithirai Festival Celebrations**
 
 
• The festival includes various rituals, processions, and cultural events, making it a vibrant and colorful celebration.
 
• Key events include the coronation of Goddess Meenakshi, her wedding ceremony, and the grand procession of Lord Alagar.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance**
 
 
• The Chithirai festival has been celebrated for centuries and is deeply rooted in the cultural and religious traditions of Tamil Nadu.
 
• It promotes the unity and cultural heritage of the region, bringing together people from different backgrounds to participate in the festivities.

questions.question: India won its first Olympic gold in hockey in which of the following years?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1928**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India won its first Olympic gold medal in hockey at the **1928 Amsterdam Olympics**.
 
• The Indian hockey team defeated the Netherlands with a score of **3-0** in the final match.
 
• The legendary player **Dhyan Chand** was a key member of the team, scoring two goals in the final.
 
• India remained unbeaten throughout the tournament, showcasing their dominance in the sport.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dhyan Chand**

 
 
• Known as the "Wizard" or "Magician" of hockey for his exceptional ball control and goal-scoring ability.
 
• Dhyan Chand played a pivotal role in India's three consecutive Olympic gold medals in 1928, 1932, and 1936.
 
• His birthday, 29th August, is celebrated as National Sports Day in India.
 
 
 
• **Field Hockey at the Olympics**
 
 
• Field hockey has been a part of the Summer Olympic Games since 1908 for men and 1980 for women.
 
• India has won a total of 8 gold medals in men's field hockey, the highest by any team in the history of the Olympics.
 
 
 
• **Hockey India**
 
 
• Hockey India is the governing body for field hockey in India.
 
• It was formed in 2009 and is affiliated with the International Hockey Federation (FIH).
 
 
 
• **Olympic Games**
 
 
• The Olympic Games are an international multi-sport event held every four years.
 
• The modern Olympics were first held in 1896 in Athens, Greece, inspired by the ancient Olympic Games held in Olympia, Greece.

questions.question: The National Food Security Act (NFSA) was enacted in which year by the Government of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2013**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The National Food Security Act (NFSA) was enacted on **10 September 2013** by the Government of India.
 
• NFSA aims to provide subsidized food grains to approximately two-thirds of India's 1.2 billion people.
 
• Under the NFSA, beneficiaries are entitled to 5 kilograms of food grains per person per month at subsidized prices.
 
• The Act covers up to 75% of the rural population and 50% of the urban population under the targeted public distribution system (TPDS).
 
• The identification of eligible households is done by the state governments, while the central government allocates food grains.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Objectives of NFSA**

 
 
• To provide food and nutritional security by ensuring access to adequate quantity of quality food at affordable prices.
 
• To ensure that the most vulnerable sections of the society receive food security.
 
 
 
• **Key Components**
 
 
• **Subsidized Food Grains:** Rice at ₹3 per kg, wheat at ₹2 per kg, and coarse grains at ₹1 per kg.
 
• **Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY):** Provides 35 kg of food grains per month to the poorest of the poor households.
 
• **Mid-Day Meal Scheme:** Provides meals to school children to improve nutritional levels.
 
 
 
• **Implementation Challenges**
 
 
• Identification of eligible beneficiaries remains a critical challenge.
 
• Leakages and inefficiencies in the public distribution system (PDS) affect the delivery of benefits.
 
 
 
• **State Involvement**
 
 
• State governments are responsible for the identification of households, issuing ration cards, and ensuring delivery of food grains.
 
• States have the flexibility to implement their own additional food security schemes.
 
 

4d:T

questions.question: Gabbro is an example of which type of rocks?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Igneous rock**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Gabbro is an example of an **intrusive igneous rock**.
 
• It is formed from the slow cooling of magma beneath the Earth's surface.
 
• Gabbro is coarse-grained and primarily composed of minerals such as pyroxene, plagioclase feldspar, and olivine.
 
• This type of rock is commonly found in the oceanic crust.
 
• Gabbro is often used in the construction industry due to its durability and strength.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Igneous Rocks**

 
 
• Formed through the cooling and solidification of magma or lava.
 
• Classified into two main types: intrusive (plutonic) and extrusive (volcanic).
 
• Common examples include basalt (extrusive) and granite (intrusive).
 
 
 
• **Sedimentary Rocks**
 
 
• Formed from the accumulation of sediments.
 
• Often contain fossils and are typically found in layers.
 
• Examples include sandstone, shale, and limestone.
 
 
 
• **Metamorphic Rocks**
 
 
• Formed from the transformation of existing rock types due to heat, pressure, and chemical processes.
 
• Examples include marble (from limestone) and schist (from shale).
 
• Metamorphic rocks can exhibit foliation or banding.
 
 
 
• **Organically Formed Sedimentary Rocks**
 
 
• Formed from the accumulation of plant or animal debris.
 
• Examples include coal (from plant material) and limestone (from shell fragments).
 
• These rocks provide valuable information about Earth's past environments.
